BACKGROUND AND SUMMARY
This application is a request for approval of a Site Plan, Conditional Use Permit and Parking
Deviation for approximately 4.2 acres located on the south side of 12300 S., at
approximately 687 W. 123000 S. (Exhibit B & C). The property is currently zoned CG. The
applicant is requesting that the Site Plan, Conditional Use Permit and Parking Deviation be
approved to allow for the development of the currently vacant site with a new building for
limited manufacturing, and limited wholesale and warehousing uses.

A majority of the subject property was rezoned to the CG zone in 2023. The City sold a
small piece of adjacent property to the company which was consolidated into the overall
parcel and subsequently rezoned to CG in 2025.

The Community Commercial land use designation is characterized as follows:




According to Draper City Municipal Code (DCMC) Section 9-8-020 the purpose of the CG
zone is to “provide areas to accommodate commercial uses which are not within shopping
centers of integrated design. This zone is intended to apply to existing "strip commercial"

developments. The zone should not be used for new commercial development unless integrated
shopping center development is not practical or desirable because of difficult size, shape,
topography, or similar problems related to land otherwise deemed to be appropriate for
commercial use. Typical uses in this zone include offices, retail stores, personal services, heavy
commercial, and institutional uses.”

Site Plan Layout. The civil site plan shows the proposed building located central to the
property with drive aisles and parking surrounding the building (Exhibit F). More extensive
landscaping is provided along the front and west sides of the property. The site contains
135 parking spaces which exceeds the maximum allowable number of spaces, hence the
additional request by the applicant for a Parking Deviation. The general site layout
complies with the requirements of the DCMC.

Circulation. The civil site plan (Exhibit F) shows internal access circling the building. On the
east a there is an existing shared access easement with the neighboring property and a
shared access drive to 12300 South is shown on the proposed site plan. Additionally, a
second vehicular access to 12300 South is included on the west side of the property. The
proposed plan provides adequate passenger vehicular circulation as well as circulation for
emergency vehicles and freight delivery vehicles.

Landscaping and Lot Coverage. The proposed landscaping plan (Exhibit G) does not comply
with the landscaping requirements of DCMC subsections 9-23-050(A)(6) and 9-23-050(G).
The use of turf grass on-site exceeds the allowable 20% limit of the overall landscape
coverage, and the staff calculated coverage at maturity is only 68% which is short of the
required 75% coverage at maturity. Staff has alerted the applicant to these deficiencies
and the applicant’s Landscape Architect is currently working on the necessary revisions to



Specialized Manufacturing                         Apps. # 2025-0123-SP, 2025-0079-USE, 2025-0219-VAR
Site Plan, CUP and Parking Deviation Requests      3
the landscape plans. Staff has included in the recommended conditions of approval that
the applicant provide the updated Landscape plans for review and approval by Planning
Staff prior to approval and issuance of the building permit.

Some of the proposed street trees are located under an existing power line are not
approved for use under power lines. The applicant is working separately with Rocky
Mountain Power to get approval to remove overhead power lines as part of the utility work
that will be necessary to provide power to the building. Should the overhead power line be
removed, there are no conflicts with the proposed street tree species for that area. If the
overhead power line is not able to be removed, alternative species would need to be on
revised plans. Staff has included in the recommended conditions of approval a condition
requiring that a street tree species approved for use under powerlines be substituted if the
applicant is ultimately unable to have the overhead power line removed.

located south of the building, and a basketball hoop in the southeast corner of the
property adjacent to the trash enclosure.

Parking Modification. Chapter 25 of the DCMC makes provisions for the Planning
Commission to authorize a deviation to the strict compliance with the terms of the Code
regarding the calculation of the minimum and maximum number of required parking
spaces. DCMC Section 9-25-090 states that the number of parking spaces may be modified
to provide flexibility beyond the 10% +/- allowed by the DCMC in order to adapt to specific
circumstances, reduce potential environmental impacts, and conserve resources. The
deviation to strict compliance is justified based upon a parking study submitted by the
applicant (Exhibit J). In order to approve a deviation to strict compliance with the parking
requirements of the DCMC, the Planning Commission must make findings based on the
type of use has outlined in DCMC Section 9-25-090(C)(4).




Specialized Manufacturing                            Apps. # 2025-0123-SP, 2025-0079-USE, 2025-0219-VAR
Site Plan, CUP and Parking Deviation Requests            5
The required parking study is included as Exhibit J of this report. Staff has reviewed the
study and has determined that it complies with the minimum requirements in ordinance to
be considered a valid study. The study concludes that the additional spaces are justified
based upon an analysis and breakdown of the individual uses including separate
calculations for the amount of office space contained within the building. Additional
analysis included demand modeling utilizing ITE Parking rates as required by ordinance.

Architecture. The architectural plans show the proposed construction of the new building
(Exhibit H). The footprint and first floor of the building is 62,524 ft2 in size. A mezzanine is
included on the west side of the building adding approximately an additional 22,343 ft2 of
floor area on the second floor.

Façade materials will be primarily architectural pre-cast concrete panels which will be
colored with admixture to the concrete and be scored and form lined per the proposed
plans. ACM metal composite panels are also included as a second primary material. The
roof will be white colored TPO roofing. Metal trim, a secondary material, will be used
minimally on all facades.

Rooftop mechanical equipment is shown screened on the north and south by a metal
screen wall approximately 6 feet in height. The proposed screening does not fully screen
the units from view as required by DCMC subsection 9-22-040(D)(3) as there is no screening
on the east or west. Additional screening of the rooftop mechanical equipment on the east
and west is still needed to comply with ordinance. Staff has included a recommended
condition of approval that the additional screening be included on revised architectural
plans prior to review and issuance of the building permit. The architectural drawings
otherwise comply with the requirements for building design found in the DCMC.

Lighting. The required lighting plans are included as Exhibit I. The maximum illumination for
the site is 8.0 foot candles with 7.0 foot candles as the maximum illumination for
pedestrian areas and 0.2 foot candles the maximum illumination allowed along the
property boundaries. The proposed lighting plan for the operational hours exceeds the
maximum allowable amounts in a few minor spots. Staff is working with the lighting
designer to reduce the intensity of the lighting in those spots, and has included as a
suggested condition of approval that revised lighting plans in compliance with ordinance
be submitted to planning staff for review and approval prior to the issuance of a building
permit.

There are also issues with the after-hours lighting plan meeting ordinance as the way that it
is currently proposed does not fully comply with ordinance requirements for the 1/3
reduction in light sources beginning at the end of the operational hours which are not
clear, but appear to be presently stated as between 6:00 am and 5:00 pm. Staff has spoken
with the lighting designer regarding the intent of the submitted after-hours lighting plan
and determined that potential minor adjustments to the plans to clarify and restate the
business operational hours as between 5:00 am and 6:00 pm would be sufficient to bring
the after hours plan into compliance with ordinance. The staff suggested condition of
approval regarding the operational hours plan also includes the needed changes to the
after-hours lighting plan. Staff also anticipates that security lighting (motion sensor) may
be desired to be incorporated into the site by the applicant. A suggested condition of



Specialized Manufacturing                            Apps. # 2025-0123-SP, 2025-0079-USE, 2025-0219-VAR
Site Plan, CUP and Parking Deviation Requests         7
approval to this effect has also been included to allow for this to be incorporated into the
revised plans if it becomes desired at a future point in time. All other aspects of the
proposed exterior lighting comply with the requirements of Chapter 9-20 of the DCMC.

Fencing. The required fencing details and locations are included on the civil site plan and
within the additional details of the civil plans (Exhibit F). The fence will be a precast
concrete fence and will be 6-feet tall along the western property lines and 8-feet tall on the
southern property line adjacent to the parking area and the city park. The proposed
fencing complies with the requirements of the DCMC.

Proposed Uses: The Conditional Use Permit request from the applicant (Exhibit K) is to allow
the building to be utilized for two potential uses listed as conditional in the CG zone. The
first requested use is limited manufacturing, and the second is limited wholesale and
warehousing. Their respective definitions from section 9-3-040 of the DCMC are as follows:

MANUFACTURING, LIMITED: An establishment engaged in the limited processing, fabrication,
assembly and/or packaging of products utilizing processes that:
  A. Have no noise, odor, vibration, or other impacts discernible outside a building; and
  B. Do not violate any applicable noise ordinance.




Specialized Manufacturing                            Apps. # 2025-0123-SP, 2025-0079-USE, 2025-0219-VAR
Site Plan, CUP and Parking Deviation Requests           8
WHOLESALE AND WAREHOUSING, LIMITED: An establishment that is engaged in the small scale
storage and sale of goods to other businesses for resale, excluding self-storage warehouses,
major distribution centers, motor freight terminals, moving and storage firms and similar high
volume, high turnover facilities. No outside storage is permitted.

The Specialized Manufacturing company is a local company that predominantly produces
custom wiring harnesses and components used in aircraft, automobile, and related
electronic industries. Their operations have no noise, odor, vibration, or other impacts that
would be discernible outside of the building. The balance of the area they will initially
occupy in the building will be their corporate offices and storage space.

The intent is that the additional area on east side of the building would be leasable space
for another business or businesses for limited warehousing or wholesaling operations. This
model allows for future potential expansion by Specialized Manufacturing into the eastern
side of the building as needed.

Anticipated detrimental impacts of the uses could include things like light spillage into
surrounding properties and an increase in freight traffic. Mitigation measures included in
the proposal include a site design that separates and directs freight traffic to enter from
the east and move immediately to the side and behind the building, also that exterior
lighting is proposed to be turned off after 6:00 pm.

Criteria For Approval.
The criteria for review and potential approval of a Site Plan request are found in Section 9-
5-090(E) of the DCMC. This section depicts the standard of review for such requests as:

         E. Standards For Approval: The following standards shall apply to the approval of a
             site plan:
            1. The entire site shall be developed at one time unless a phased development
               plan is approved.
            2. A site plan shall conform to applicable standards set forth in this title, including
               but not limited to, building heights, setbacks, access points, parking,
               landscaping, and building materials.
            3. The proposed development plans meet the intent, goals, and objectives of the
               general plan and the purpose of the zone district in which the site is located.
            4. The public facilities and services in the area are adequate to support the
               subject development, as required by engineering standards and specifications.
            5. The proposed development plans comply with the engineering standards
               found in Titles 7, 8, 11, 12, 16, and 18 of this code, including traffic, storm water
               drainage, and utilities concerns.




Specialized Manufacturing                        Apps. # 2025-0123-SP, 2025-0079-USE, 2025-0219-VAR
Site Plan, CUP and Parking Deviation Requests     9
The criteria for review and potential approval of a Conditional Use Permit request are
found in Section 9-5-080(E) of the DCMC. This section depicts the standard of review for
such requests as:

         E. Approval Standards: The standards of this subsection shall apply to the issuance of a
             conditional use permit:
          1. A conditional use permit may be issued for a use to be located within a zone where
             the particular conditional use is allowed by the use regulations of the zone.
          2. Reasonable conditions may be imposed as necessary to substantially mitigate
             reasonably anticipated detrimental effects of the proposed use. These conditions may
             include conditions concerning use, construction, character, location, landscaping,
             screening, parking, hours of operation, and other matters relating to the purposes
             and objectives of this section. Such conditions shall be expressly set forth in the
             motion authorizing the conditional use permit.
          3. If the reasonably anticipated detrimental effects of a proposed conditional use
             cannot be substantially mitigated by the imposition of reasonable conditions to
             achieve compliance with applicable standards, the conditional use may be denied.
          4. The following factors shall be reviewed and considered in determining whether a
             conditional use permit application should be approved, approved with conditions, or
             denied because reasonable conditions cannot be imposed to achieve compliance with
             applicable standards:
               a. The harmony and compliance of the proposed use with the objectives and
                   requirements of the city's general plan and this title;
               b. The suitability of the specific property for the proposed use;
               c. Whether the proposed use or facility may be injurious to potential or existing
                   development in the vicinity;
               d. The economic impact of the proposed facility or use on the surrounding area;
               e. The aesthetic impact of the proposed facility or use on the surrounding area;
               f. The safeguards proposed or provided to ensure adequate utilities, transportation
                   access, drainage, parking, loading space, lighting, screening, landscaping, open
                   space, fire protection, and pedestrian and vehicular circulation;
               g. The safeguards provided or proposed to prevent noxious or offensive emissions
                   such as noise, glare, dust, pollutants and odor from the proposed facility or use;
                   and
               h. The impact of the proposed facility or use on the health, safety, and welfare of the
                   city, the area, and persons owning or leasing property in the area.
          5. The planning commission may request additional information as may be reasonably
             needed to determine whether the requirements of this subsection E can be met.

The criteria for review and potential approval of a Parking Deviation are found in Section 9-
25-090(C)(4) of the DCMC. This section depicts the standard of review of such request as:




Specialized Manufacturing                         Apps. # 2025-0123-SP, 2025-0079-USE, 2025-0219-VAR
Site Plan, CUP and Parking Deviation Requests     10
        a. For commercial, retail, office, and mixed use developments, the planning commission
           must find that:
              (1) Adequate parking will be provided;
              (2) The total number of spaces that would otherwise be required for each individual
                 establishment in the development is overly burdensome for the site specific
                 factors of the application;
              (3) Estimated trade offs between businesses which are open when others are closed
                 will not overburden the parking provided;
              (4) There is an adequate availability of approved on street or shared parking for all
                 associated uses;
              (5) Site or use specific conditions or factors do not provide for compliance with the
                 parking calculation used or parking requirements outlined in section 9-25-100,
                 table 9-25-1 of this chapter;
              (6) Transportation alternatives, including proximity to transit stations, provide
                 adequate transportation to offset any reduction in parking; and
              (7) Any potential for future expansion or addition to the development will have or
                 will provide adequate parking for that expansion or addition;
              (8) ADA compliant parking requirements are not proposed for adjustment.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Planning Commission review the request based on the findings
listed below and the criteria for approval, or denial as listed within the staff report. The
Planning Commission should also review the request, hear from the applicant, and receive
public comment prior to making a decision.

If the Planning Commission decides to approve the request, staff recommends they include
the following conditions of approval:

         1.       That all requirements of the Draper City Engineering, Public Works, Building,
                  Planning, and Fire Divisions are satisfied throughout the development of the
                  site and the construction of all buildings on the site, including permitting.
         2.       That all requirements of the geotechnical report are satisfied throughout the
                  development of the site and the construction of all buildings on the site.
         3.       That that the applicant provides updated Landscaping plans for review and
                  approval by Planning Staff for compliance with ordinance requirements prior
                  to approval and issuance of the building permit.
         4.       That if the overhead power line along the front of the property is not
                  removed, that the proposed street trees beneath the power line must be
                  replaced with a species from the city approved list for use under power lines.
         5.       That proof of UDOT approval for access onto 12300 South must be provided
                  to staff prior to issuance of a land disturbance permit or building permit.
                  Development of the frontage must also comply with any requirements
                  imposed by UDOT.
         6.       That revised architectural plans and elevations be submitted detailing the
                  necessary additional screening of the rooftop mechanical systems for review
                  and approval by planning staff prior to review and issuance of the building
                  permit.
         7.       That revised lighting plans in compliance with the requirements of the DCMC
                  be submitted to planning staff for review and approval prior to the issuance
                  of a building permit.
         8.       That all exterior lighting shall be turned off between the hours of 6:00 pm

         9.       That a separate security lighting plan in compliance with the requirements

                  lighting to the site.

Fire Division Review.

       1.      Fire Department Access is required. An unobstructed minimum road width
               of twenty-six (26) feet exclusive of the shoulders and a minimum height of
               thirteen (13) feet six (6) inches shall be required. The road must be designed
               and maintained to support the imposed loads of emergency apparatus. The
               surface shall be able to provide all weather driving capabilities. The road shall
               have an inside turning radius of twenty – eight (28) feet. There shall be a
               maximum grade of 10%. Grades may be checked prior to building permits
               being issued.
       2.      Fire Hydrants are required. Hydrants are required for this project. They
               shall be protected with bollards if susceptible to vehicle damage. Based on
               the square footage of this building the code states that it will need 6 hydrants
               with fire sprinklers that can be reduced to three. The required fire flow for
               the building is 5250gpm and with a 50% reduction for fire sprinklers the fire
               flow would then be 2625gpm. One of the hydrants will need to be located to
               be with 100 feet of the Fire Department Connection.
       3.      Hydrants and Site Access. All hydrants and a form of acceptable temporary
               Fire Department Access to the site shall be installed and APPROVED by the
               Fire Department prior to the issuance of any Building Permits. If at any time
               during the building phase any of the hydrants or temporary Fire Department
               Access becomes non-compliant any and all permits could be revoked.
       4.      Utilities. All utilities including Fire hydrants within the required width of fire
               apparatus access roads shall be installed prior to introducing combustible
               materials to a site or commencing vertical construction. Any excavation in the
               required fire department access roadway after combustible materials are on
               site shall be performed in a manner to maintain access to the site and shall
               be coordinated with the Fire Marshal. Combustible material shall not be
               placed in any way that will impede fire apparatus access to any site.
5.   Site Access Required During Construction. Prior to and throughout
     construction a form of acceptable temporary Fire Department Access to the
     site shall be installed this includes turn arounds. The required access for fire
     apparatus access shall have a base material capable of supporting a
     75,000lbs vehicle, during most-weather conditions, installed and compacted
     to 95% relative compaction at a minimum of 26 feet wide. There shall be no
     parking of construction vehicles, sub-contractor vehicles within the required
     fire access they shall be parked on the non-hydrant side of the road to allow
     for emergency vehicles to still access the project. If at any time during the
     building phase any of the hydrants or temporary Fire Department Access
     becomes non-compliant any and all permits could be revoked.
6.   Access and Fire Protection During Construction All buildings under
     construction shall meet the requirements of IFC Chapter 33, Fire Safety
     During Construction and Demolition as well as all of the sections detailed in
     this document.
7.   IFC SECTION 3310 ACCESS FOR FIRE FIGHTING DURING CONSTRUCTION
     3310.1.1 Required access. Approved vehicle access for firefighting shall be,
     provided to all construction or demolition sites. Vehicle access shall be
     provided to within 100 feet (30 480 mm) of temporary or permanent fire
     department connections. Either temporary or permanent roads, capable of
     supporting vehicle loading under all weather conditions, shall provide vehicle
     access. Vehicle access shall be, maintained until permanent fire apparatus
     access roads are available.
             ❖ Until permanent fire apparatus access roads are constructed, fire-
             fighting vehicle access is the means by which fire fighters gain access
             to the construction or demolition site and building for fire
             suppression and rescue operations. Such access is an integral
             component of the fire prevention program. The site superintendent
             or other person responsible for construction and demolition
             operations is responsible for maintaining and policing fire-fighter
             access routes, as pro-vided in Section 3308. Fire apparatus must be
             able to get within 100 feet (30 480 mm) of any installed fire
             department connection supplying water to temporary or permanent
             fire protection systems. Access roads must support the weight of the
             heaviest vehicle that might respond. The weight requirements are
             available from the local fire department. All-weather sur-faces are
             required because the responding fire department should not waste
             time moving snow or trying to get out of mud.
8.   IFC 3315.1 Completion before Occupancy. In buildings where an automatic
     sprinkler system is required by this code or the IBC, it shall be unlawful to
     occupy any portion of a building or structure until the automatic sprinkler
     system installation has been tested and approved except as provided in
     section 105.3.4 of the IFC.
9.    IFC 3315.2 Operation of Valves. Operation of sprinkler control valves shall
      be allowed only by properly authorized personnel and shall be accompanied
      by notification of duly designated parties. Where the sprinkler protection is
      being regularly turned off and on facilitate connection of newly completed
      segments, the sprinkler control valves shall be checked at the end of each
      work period to ascertain that protection is in service.
10.   IFC 3316.1 Structures under construction, alteration or demolition shall be
      provided with not less than one approved portable fire extinguisher in
      accordance with Section 906 and sized for not less than ordinary hazard as
      follows: 1. At each stairway on all floor levels where combustible materials
      have accumulated. 2. In every storage and construction shed. 3. Additional
      portable fire extinguishers shall be provided where special hazards exist
      including, but not limited to, the storage and use of flammable and
      combustible liquids.
11.   IFC 3313.1 An approved water supply for fire protection, either temporary or
      permanent, shall be made available as soon as combustible building
      materials arrive on the site, on commencement of vertical combustible
      construction and on installation of a standpipe system in buildings under
      construction
12.   No combustible construction shall be allowed prior to hydrant installation
      and testing by water purveyor. All hydrants must be operational prior to any
      combustible elements being received or delivered on building site.
13.   Fire Department Connection Location. The FDC shall be on the North side
      of the building and shall be located and arranged so that hose lines can be
      readily and conveniently attached to the inlets without interference from any
      nearby objects including but not limited to buildings, fences, posts, and
      landscaping.
14.   Fire Sprinklers Required. A deferred submittal for a NFPA 13 fire sprinkler
      shop drawings are to be sent via email to: fire.permits@draperutah.gov . A
      complete set of plans, with manufacturer cut sheets, and hydraulic
      calculations. Plans must be stamped by a NICET level III or better in Auto
      Sprinkler Layout. (There needs to be a hydrant with-in a 100 feet of the FDC.)
      FDC is required to have KNOX Locking Caps. ALL FIRE PROTECTION PLANS
      REQUIRE 3rd PARTY REVIEW PRIOR TO BE SUBMITTED TO THE DRAPER FIRE
      DEPARTMENT.
15.   Standpipes May Be Required. This building may be required to have
      standpipes. This standpipe will be required to be pressure tested and a
      Contractor Certificate of Completion will be required to be filled out.
16.   Fire Alarm Required. A deferred submittal for fire alarm shop drawings are to
      be sent via email to the following to: fire.permits@draperutah.gov A
      complete set of plans, with manufacturer cut sheets, and battery
      calculations. Plans must be stamped by a NICET level III or better in Fire
      Alarm Systems. ALL FIRE ALARM PLANS REQUIRE 3rd PARTY REVIEW PRIOR
                TO BE SUBMITTED TO THE DRAPER FIRE DEPARTMENT.
       17.      Emergency Responder Radio Coverage Required. Emergency responder
                radio coverage shall be provided in accordance with the IFC 510. Before a
                Fire Safety Codes Release (Certificate of Occupancy) is issued, compliance
                with International Fire Code Section 510 is required by means of an
                Emergency Responder Radio Coverage System (ERRCS) installed, tested, and
                accepted OR through field testing by a FCC licensed radio contractor to verify
                that an ERRCS is not warranted. A critical element to compliance with this
                standard is preliminary testing once the building is dried-in.
       18.      Knox Boxes Required. Fire Department “Knox Brand” lock box to be
                mounted to exterior walls, near the main entrance and/or nearest the door
                serving the exterior access to the fire sprinkler riser room. (At a height of 5
                feet to the top of the box) Lock box purchase can be arranged by the General
                Contractor.
       19.      2A-10BC Fire Extinguishers required. The extinguisher needs to be a
                serviceable type meaning metal head and metal neck. Extinguishers need to
                be located in a conspicuous location where they will be readily accessible and
                immediately available for use. Placed every 75 feet of travel. If in cabinet or
                not the extinguisher or cabinet needs to be mounted so that the top is not
                more than five (5) feet above the floor.
       20.      Visible Addressing Required. New and existing buildings shall have
                approved address numbers plainly legible and visible from the street
                fronting the property. These numbers shall contrast with their background.

   EXHIBIT J
PARKING STUDY
                                     MEMORANDUM

Date:          September 5, 2025
                                                                                NO. 12890754
                                                                                   Jordi J.
To:            Draper City                                                         Berrett
                                                                                      09/05/2025
From:          Hales Engineering


Subject:       Draper Specialized Manufacturing Parking Study
                                                                                               UT25-3001


Introduction

This memorandum discusses the parking study completed for the proposed Specialized
Manufacturing development located in Draper, Utah. The study identifies the City parking supply
rates and parking demand rates calculated from local data. The proposed development is located
on the south side of 12300 South near 700 West. A vicinity map of the project site is shown in
Figure 1.




                  Figure 1: Site vicinity map of the project in Draper, Utah

                      1220 North 500 West, Ste. 202 Lehi, UT 84043   p 801.766.4343
                                     www.halesengineering.com
Project Description

A supply of 135 stalls is currently planned for the project. A site plan is provided in Appendix A.
The following land uses are included in the proposed project:

    •   Manufacturing                                                            37,980 sq. ft.
    •   Office Space                                                             19,684 sq. ft.
    •   Warehousing                                                              23,528 sq. ft.

It is anticipated that 11,100 sq. ft. of the total office space will be leased. The rest of the building
will be used for Specialized Manufacturing offices, manufacturing, and warehousing.

City Parking Code

From discussions with City staff, it is understood that the predominant land use parking rate
should be used for the development’s overall square footage. Using that assumption, the City
would use the manufacturing parking stall rate of 1.0 stall/KSF. As such, the City requires 82
parking stalls for the 81,192 sq. ft. building.

However, in section 9-25-060 in the City code, it is stated that individual parking rates should be
applied to each land use to calculate a parking stall count for the development. Hales Engineering
calculated the required parking stalls using the method described in the City code.

The Draper City code specifies parking rates for various land use types. The required parking
rates found in the City code for the study land uses are shown in Table 1. The calculations for the
parking required by the City are shown in Table 2. As shown, it is anticipated that the City would
require 129 stalls for the proposed development.

                                    Table 1: City Parking Rates

                                                      Unit     Rate (stalls
                                 Land Use
                                                      Type      per unit)
                               Manufacturing                       1.00
                               General Office          KSF         4.00
                               Warehousing                         0.5
                           Source: Draper City code, 2025




                        1220 North 500 West, Ste. 202 Lehi, UT 84043     p 801.766.4343
                                       www.halesengineering.com
                              Table 2: City Parking Calculations
                                    City Parking Calculations
                           Draper - Specialized Manufacturing PS
                                            # of   Unit Rate (stalls      Total
                        Land Use
                                           Units   Type  per unit)        Stalls
                   Manufacturing           37.98              1.00          38
                   General Office          19.68   KSF        4.00          79
                   Warehousing             23.53              0.50          12
                       TOTAL                                                129
                 Source: Draper City code, 2025.


Local Parking Demand

Hales Engineering collected data on August 26, 2025, from the existing Specialized
Manufacturing building located at 12875 Minuteman Drive in Draper, Utah. Currently, Specialized
Manufacturing occupies all 31,651 square feet of space which consists of manufacturing, office,
and warehousing space. The counts were collected during the peak hour between 10:00 a.m. and
12:00 p.m. per discussions with the client. During that time, there was a maximum of 46 parking
stalls occupied. Two of those parking stalls are used for the driving school. As such, 44 parking
stalls were in use by Specialized Manufacturing. This is equivalent to a rate of 1.39 stalls/KSF.

The current Specialized Manufacturing site already includes internal offices and warehouse space
used for their operations. As such, the parking rate calculated was applied to their manufacturing,
warehousing, and office space in the proposed project land uses. The additional leasable office
space will be used by other businesses and was calculated separately using the 85th percentile
rate published in the Institute of Transportation Engineers (ITE), Parking Generation (6th Edition,
2023).

The number of stalls needed based on these rates is shown in Table 3. It is anticipated that the
parking demand for the proposed project will be 130 parking stalls using the local rate for the
project land uses.

Since the ITE rates represent actual parking demand, it is common to provide a parking supply
beyond what the anticipated demand is to accommodate occasional surges in demand and to
reduce the need for drivers to circle the parking lot to find an open stall. Hales Engineering
recommends providing 5% additional stalls beyond the anticipated demand. Therefore, a supply
of 137 parking stalls should be provided.




                       1220 North 500 West, Ste. 202 Lehi, UT 84043   p 801.766.4343
                                      www.halesengineering.com
                         Table 3: Local and ITE Parking Generation

                            Local Parking Demand and Supply

                                       Units Type    Rate                                   (+5%)
        Specialized Manufacturing      70.08                1.39                97          102
                                                KSF
        General Office (710)           11.11                2.98                33           35
                 TOTAL                                                         130          137
                                                                   th
      Source: Hales Engineering, 2025; ITE Parking Generation, 6        Edition, 2023


Comparison and Recommendation

A comparison of the proposed supply, the local parking demand, the city’s parking requirement,
and the recommended supply based on the ITE Parking Generation rates is shown in Table 4.
Based on the provided information, Hales Engineering recommends that 137 stalls be provided
for the project.

                                 Table 4: Parking Comparison
                                    Source                      # of Stalls
                             Proposed Site Plan                         135
                              City Requirement                          129
                        Local Parking Demand + 5%                       137


Conclusions

The key findings of this study are as follows:
   • City code requires fewer stalls than the actual parking demand at the current Specialized
      Manufacturing site, and as such it is recommended that the local parking rate be used to
      provide an adequate amount of parking stalls
   • A supply of 137 parking stalls is anticipated to be sufficient to accommodate the parking
      demand of the proposed project.

If you have any questions regarding this memorandum, please contact us at 801.766.4343.

APPLICANT CUP AND DEVIATION REQUEST RESPONSES
Concord Properties

7/18/25

               Project Narrative – New Specialized Building
Applicant & Property Information

      Applicant Name: Concord Properties

      Tenant Name: Specialized Manufacturing

      Proposed Address: 687 W 12300 S, Draper, Utah 84020

      Parcel Number: 27-25-302-023

      Property Size: Approximately 4.20 acres

      Current Use: Vacant land

      Proposed Use: Limited Manufacturing, Wholesale, and Warehousing

      Zoning: CG and RA2. It is understood that the RA2 zoned area needs to be rezoned
       before Site Plan and CUP approval



Project Description

Concord Properties, along with Specialized Manufacturing, is seeking a Conditional Use
Permit to construct and operate a new limited manufacturing, wholesale, and warehousing
facility on the 4.20-acre parcel located at 687 W 12300 S in Draper, Utah. This project
involves the construction of a new building similar in design and functionality to our current
facility at 12875 S. Minuteman Drive, also located in Draper.

The proposed use is consistent with limited manufacturing, wholesale, and warehousing
and will involve no outdoor storage, no hazardous materials, and no signiﬁcant emissions
such as noise, dust, or odors. The operations will be conducted entirely indoors in a clean,
professional environment.



Operations

      Hours of Operation:

          o   Monday–Thursday: 7:00 AM – 5:00 PM
          o   Friday: 7:00 AM – 12:00 PM

      Initial Sta ing: Approximately 60–70 employees

      Future Sta ing: Projected growth to 150 employees over the next 5–10 years

      Customer/Client Tra ic: Minimal — estimated 5–10 visits per month

      Deliveries/Shipments: Daily; standard commercial vehicle access

      Noise/Odors/Emissions: None anticipated

      Hazardous Materials: None stored or used onsite



Site Design & Infrastructure

The site will be developed to accommodate all required parking, internal circulation, and
delivery needs. Approximately 60–80 vehicles are expected on-site daily at initial operation,
with future capacity expansion planned. The site design will include:

      Adequate onsite parking for employees and occasional visitors

      Exterior lighting and fencing for safety and security

      Tie-in to UDOT’s stormwater drainage system, with onsite stormwater detention
       incorporated into the plan

      Landscaping and building aesthetics in keeping with surrounding commercial
       development

      The project is not anticipated to signiﬁcantly impact the current ﬂow of tra ic on
       12300 South or surrounding roads. Deliveries and employee tra ic will be spread
       out throughout the day, and no signiﬁcant congestion is expected.



Compatibility with Surrounding Uses

The surrounding area includes:

      Residential uses to the west and north (low-density)

      Commercial developments to the north and east

      Public uses to the south
The proposed limited manufacturing, wholesale, and warehousing use is highly compatible
with these surroundings. The design, operation, and tra ic generated by Specialized Mfg.
will be appropriate for the neighborhood and contribute positively to the area’s ongoing
development.
Concord Properties

7/18/25

                  Statement of Compliance with Approval Standards

This application for a Conditional Use Permit for Specialized Mfg. demonstrates full
compliance with the applicable approval standards outlined in DCMC 9-5-080(E). The
proposed use of the site at 687 W 12300 S for limited manufacturing, wholesale, and
warehousing meets all criteria required for CUP consideration:

   1. Zoning Compatibility: The proposed use is conditionally permitted within the CG
      (General Commercial) zone and does not require a variance. The use complies with
      all relevant zoning provisions, including site layout, building design, and operational
      intent.

   2. Reasonable Conditions for Mitigation: Although no detrimental impacts are
      anticipated, the applicant is prepared to comply with all reasonable conditions
      deemed necessary by the Planning Commission to mitigate potential effects,
      including site lighting, fencing, and landscaping buffers.

   3. Detrimental Impacts Can Be Substantially Mitigated: No detrimental impacts are
      expected that cannot be addressed through site design and operational standards.
      The use will generate low-intensity traffic, include no hazardous materials, and
      maintain clean indoor operations.

   4. Evaluation of Required Factors:

          o   General Plan Compliance: The proposed use aligns with Draper City's
              General Plan by supporting economic development and providing
              employment opportunities within a mixed commercial zone.

          o   Site Suitability: The 4.20-acre lot is well-suited for a limited manufacturing,
              wholesale, and warehousing use, with ample space for building, parking,
              circulation, and stormwater detention.

          o   No Injury to Adjacent Development: The business is not expected to cause
              injury to existing or potential development. Operations are fully enclosed,
              quiet, and low-impact.

          o   Positive Economic Impact: The development will create jobs, generate
              property tax revenue, and support the local economy.
o   Minimal Aesthetic Impact: The building will match the quality and character
    of nearby commercial structures, with professional landscaping and
    screened areas.

o   Adequate Services and Infrastructure:

       1. Utilities – The site is currently served by all necessary utilities,
          including culinary water, sanitary sewer, storm drain, power, natural
          gas, and telecommunications. No off-site utility upgrades are
          required.

       2. Transportation Access – Vehicular access is provided via 12300
          South, a public right-of-way with sufficient capacity for daily traffic
          and delivery needs. Access points are located to maximize site
          circulation and minimize impacts on adjacent properties.

       3. Drainage – Site will tie-in to UDOT’s stormwater drainage system and
          will includes on-site stormwater detention. The on-site detention
          system is designed to prevent runoff impacts to neighboring parcels
          or public infrastructure.

       4. Parking – The site includes 129 standard and 6 ADA-compliant
          parking stalls, meeting Draper City’s minimum parking requirements
          for the intended use. Spaces are distributed to support both
          employee and visitor access.

       5. Loading Space – A dedicated loading zone is provided on the South
          side of the site, with direct access to the building for daily deliveries
          and service vehicles. The loading area is separated from general
          parking and circulation paths for safety and efficiency.

       6. Lighting – All exterior lighting will be downward-facing and shielded to
          minimize light spill onto adjacent properties. A photometric plan
          demonstrating compliance has been submitted through the Site Plan
          Application.

       7. Screening – Mechanical equipment, refuse containers, and loading
          areas will be screened using fencing and/or landscaping in
          accordance with City standards, ensuring visual compatibility with
          surrounding uses.

       8. Landscaping & Open Space – The landscaping plan meets or
          exceeds City requirements, including street frontage plantings,
                     interior landscaping islands, and screening vegetation. All landscaped
                     areas will be irrigated and maintained.

                 9. Fire Protection – The site and building layout have been reviewed for
                    emergency access. Required fire lanes, hydrants, and clearances are
                    included in the site design per International Fire Code standards.

                 10. Pedestrian & Vehicular Circulation – Internal drive aisles, sidewalks,
                     and parking layouts are designed for clear and safe circulation for
                     vehicles and pedestrians. Direct pedestrian access is provided
                     between parking areas and building entrances.

          o   No Noxious Emissions: Operations will not produce dust, noise, pollutants,
              or odors. No hazardous materials will be stored or used on-site.

          o   Positive Health, Safety, and Welfare Impact: The proposed use will
              contribute to the welfare of the community through thoughtful development,
              job creation, and responsible design.

The applicant affirms that all applicable City, State, and Federal regulations will be
followed and that the project can operate in full compliance with Draper City's standards
for conditional use approval.
